advancements.nookofthedead.close_call.de: Hold the infection back with under a minute left
advancements.nookofthedead.cured.title: Back to Their Senses
advancements.nookofthedead.familiar_face: Kill one of them that was a player
advancements.nookofthedead.first_dose.de: Hold the infection back with a suppressant
advancements.nookofthedead.institute_map: Put a map together from its scraps
advancements.nookofthedead.put_down.desc: Throw a suppressant at a Mutated Zombie
advancements.nookofthedead.root.descript: Step into the fallen world through the If
advancements.nookofthedead.root.title: A World Gone Wrong
Sleep through a night in the fallen world
advancements.nookofthedead.vandal.title: At the Bottom of It
diary.nookofthedead.1.1: Day three. They shut the east gate. The people from outside are kept in tents in the square. Anyone with a fever is taken to another building. Nobody says where.
diary.nookofthedead.1.2: All night, screaming beyond the gate. By morning it was quiet. The guard said it was over. He would not look at me.
diary.nookofthedead.2.1: My brother was bitten. He hid it under his sleeve, but I knew. The fever is rising; he keeps asking for water. The apothecary was already empty.
diary.nookofthedead.2.2: I nailed boards over his door. Something inside keeps knocking. I call his name. Nothing answers.
diary.nookofthedead.3.1: Ten days of smoke from the tower. No answering smoke, not once. Maybe there is no one left in the next town, or the one after.
diary.nookofthedead.3.2: Keep the lights burning. They do not appear where it is roofed and bright. That is the one thing I still believe.
diary.nookofthedead.4.1: One vial left. There should be more in the storehouse across the street. But there are more of them out there than yesterday. Tonight, or tomorrow? Nothing promises that tomorrow I will still be me.
diary.nookofthedead.5.1: In the square I saw people who call it salvation. They knelt before the bitten ones, singing.
diary.nookofthedead.5.2: Do not open the door. Three are still in the storehouse below. Even if we do not come back, do not open the door.
message.nookofthedead.dying: Your body will not obey you...
message.nookofthedead.dowsing: The rod pulls hard - something lies about %s blocks off.
block.nookofthedead.vaccine.resumed: The vaccine is going out again.
block.nookofthedead.vaccine.confirm:
Stop the machine and the mutation will begin to spread again, and the world may fill with the dead once more.

Stop it?
film.nookofthedead.opening.2: The world of what-if that everyone wishes for.
film.nookofthedead.opening.3: By the magic of the mirror, another Overworld, untouched, spreads out before you...
film.nookofthedead.ending.title: Nook of the Dead
film.nookofthedead.ending.author: made by Riftwright
film.nookofthedead.ending.1: From the top of the tower the vaccine's mist went out on the wind, until it covered the world.
film.nookofthedead.ending.2: The dead it touched caught fire, and one by one they fell.
film.nookofthedead.ending.3: The mutation that moved them has quieted. While the machine on the tower keeps the mist going, they will not rise again.
film.nookofthedead.ending.4: The ruined town stays ruined. What was lost will not come back.
film.nookofthedead.ending.5: And yet - the rebuilding of this world begins here.
book.nookofthedead.refuge_note:
If you have come this far, you must have put him to rest, in the hall. Thank you.
We are leaving the ground. The Lode Pearls left over, we leave for whoever comes after.
Do not let the fire of humankind go out.
diary.nookofthedead.6.1: The cows stopped grazing. They stand at the fence all day, facing the house. Father says it is the heat.
diary.nookofthedead.6.2: Father went out to the barn with the lamp. I heard the boards break. I burned it, with all of them inside. I could not do anything else.
diary.nookofthedead.7.1: We raised the wall another three blocks. The machines in the hall still turn, sorting ore no one will ever smelt. I leave them running. The noise feels like company.
diary.nookofthedead.8.1: Sealed carts came up the north road again tonight, without lanterns. The institute gates opened and closed. Nobody in the town talks about it.
diary.nookofthedead.8.2: At dawn a man came down the institute road carrying a case he would not put down. He did not stop at the inn, and nobody saw him again. The fevers began the week after.
diary.nookofthedead.9.1: Mama says play quietly. They hear everything, even through the walls. I may only walk on the carpet. I drew a picture of the sun. I have not seen it in a long time.
diary.nookofthedead.10.1: We went down into the old galleries. None of them walk down here. Food for a month, if we are careful. The children sleep for the first time in weeks.
diary.nookofthedead.10.2: Something knocks on the shaft cover at night. Three knocks, then nothing. Hanna says it is the wind. There is no wind down here.
diary.nookofthedead.11.1: The suppressant buys hours, not days. We give it to the ones who can still hold a cup. The ward upstairs is locked. Do not answer when they call your name.
diary.nookofthedead.12.1: The last train did not come. We waited on the platform until dark, all of us with our bags. Then the ones from the tunnel came instead.
diary.nookofthedead.13.1: To buy: three bundles of wheat, six eggs, two candles. Red thread. Shoelaces for Mina. Return the baker's basket - it has been a week.
diary.nookofthedead.14.1: Ward rota. Day 1: Marta, Ilse, Peter, Johan, me. Day 3: Marta, Ilse, Peter, me. Day 5: Ilse, Peter, me.
diary.nookofthedead.14.2: Day 7: Ilse, me. Day 9: me. Day 11:
diary.nookofthedead.15.1: Today I gave Biscuit a bone. He can sit. He can't shake hands yet. Papa says he is too old to learn. I am going to teach him anyway.
diary.nookofthedead.15.2: Biscuit is not allowed on my bed. But when Mama is asleep, he is. Secret.
diary.nookofthedead.16.1: Sunny. The carrots are all up. The potatoes, not yet. A shower toward evening. The beetroot row keeps holding water; tomorrow, one more ditch.
diary.nookofthedead.17.1: Checkpoint duty, second week. Before anyone passes, I look at their arms and neck. No sleeve rolled up, no entry. Today forty-two let through, six turned back.
diary.nookofthedead.17.2: The line outside the barrier is a little shorter every morning. Fewer coming, or fewer able to come. I have decided not to ask.
diary.nookofthedead.18.1: Grandmother's pumpkin pie. One pumpkin, a spoon of sugar, one egg. Keep the furnace low. Do not cut it as soon as it is done. Waiting for it to cool is the hardest part.
diary.nookofthedead.18.2: Beside the recipe, in Mother's hand: "Bake two. One is for next door."
diary.nookofthedead.19.1: Mill rota. Mon: Tomas. Tue: me. Wed: Eda. Thu: Tomas. Fri: me (swapped with Eda, her boy's birthday). Sat: closed. Sacks from the north shelf. Oil the millstone on Tuesdays.
diary.nookofthedead.20.1: Three days indoors for the sandstorm. Cloth stuffed in the window gaps, and still sand on the floor every morning. The dig at the pyramid has stopped.
diary.nookofthedead.20.2: After the storm I walked out to the dig. The scaffold was buried, the tents empty, the tools left where they lay. The entrance had been blocked from the inside.
diary.nookofthedead.21.1: Dear Rina. How is the new town? Nothing changes here. The baker's nephew lives in your house now. He keeps flowers on the sill, in the same spot you did.
diary.nookofthedead.21.2: I wrote this, then forgot what I meant to say. I will write again another time.
diary.nookofthedead.22.1: Oak planks, 64 x3. Spruce, 64 x1 - not enough. Stairs 40. Glass panes 12 (plus 2 for the ones I broke). Roof next week. The owner wants something brighter. Birch, maybe.
diary.nookofthedead.23.1: Errands. 1. Twenty glass bottles. 2. A new logbook. 3. Report to the director re: ■■■■. 4. Letter to my wife - not home this week either. 5. Return the north gate key.
diary.nookofthedead.24.1: Morning, at the bend in the river. Three cod, one salmon. One boot. Another boot. Somebody upstream keeps losing boots.
diary.nookofthedead.25.1: Noa turned seven. He blew out every candle on the cake in one go. His present was a fishing rod. He is already fishing in the water trough. I told him there is nothing in it. He won't listen.
diary.nookofthedead.26.1: We moved down into the cellar. Only two beds fit. The children sleep two to a bed. Every window upstairs is boarded.
diary.nookofthedead.26.2: At every meal someone goes up to the kitchen to fetch things. Fourteen steps. The first one creaks, so we step over it.
diary.nookofthedead.27.1: Bern next door moved the fence one block onto our side again. I measured. No mistake. Two rows of our carrots are in his garden now.
diary.nookofthedead.27.2: Went over in the evening. He was coughing and asked if it could wait. The fence stays where it is. Fine. Tomorrow.
diary.nookofthedead.28.1: The black cat came again. In through the kitchen window, asleep in front of the furnace. I have decided not to name it. Once you name it, it is yours. It may be too late for that already.
diary.nookofthedead.29.1: We took the lift to the very top of the tower. The air up there is thin and cold. The town below looks like a model of itself.
diary.nookofthedead.29.2: Someone said nothing can reach us up here. Two weeks of food. We have agreed the lift will not go back down.
diary.nookofthedead.30.1: First snow. The roofs are white. The children built a snowman: coal for eyes, a carrot for a nose. Overnight somebody put a pumpkin on its head.
diary.nookofthedead.31.1: I am setting Mother's favourite song into note blocks. Twenty-three clicks to get one note right. Today I found out the block underneath changes the sound.
diary.nookofthedead.31.2: The first eight bars are done. I played them for Mother. She asked what song it was. More practice.
diary.nookofthedead.32.1: Signal lamp log. Six o'clock: signalled the tower across the way. No answer. Noon: again. I think a window over there lit once. Six in the evening: no answer.
diary.nookofthedead.32.2: Second day. At night the lamp on the tower across the way blinks. In the same order as yesterday, over and over. When I answer, it does not stop.
diary.nookofthedead.33.1: The shed key is gone. Coat pocket, no. Kitchen, no. Edge of the well, no. Last saw it while feeding the goat. The goat looks like it knows something.
diary.nookofthedead.34.1: Harvest fair. Stalls all across the square. The biggest pumpkin went to Elma's family again; ours came third. Jonas won the melon-eating contest two years running.
diary.nookofthedead.34.2: At night we all danced under the lanterns. Fewer people than last year, I think. The farms up north did not come.
diary.nookofthedead.35.1: The new house. The windows face south; in the morning the sun reaches all the way to the kitchen. Upstairs is only a floor so far. One bed carried in and the room is full.
diary.nookofthedead.35.2: First night. So many sounds I don't know: the mill wheel, the dog next door, the weathervane. Soon they will all be the sounds of home.
diary.nookofthedead.36.1: The 19th. Still here. The 20th. Still here. The 21st. Still here.
diary.nookofthedead.37.1: Third day through the mirror. This is not the world we were told about.
diary.nookofthedead.37.2: The mirror home was smashed yesterday. They crowded in front of it and beat on it, as if trying to see through to the other side.
diary.nookofthedead.38.1: The night sounds different. No rattle of bones any more, no hissing. Only running feet.
diary.nookofthedead.39.1: A cart from the institute came to the square and handed out the medicine, one bottle each. Pale green, with a faint smell of iron. Nobody answered those who asked what it was made from.
diary.nookofthedead.40.1: Ten days since we shut the door. He beats on it from the hall, day and night. The iron will hold. Our nerves will give out first.
diary.nookofthedead.40.2: When the beating stops, nobody sleeps at all. When it starts again, someone in the bunks counts the blows under their breath, and the rest of us count along.
diary.nookofthedead.41.1: In here the clocks go on, but the one in the body does not. We do not know why yet. Not knowing, we change the mixture again: the thirty-first time.
diary.nookofthedead.41.2: The chief has rigged the door: once Seven is asleep, it opens by itself. I asked who it was for. Not for us, the chief said.
diary.nookofthedead.42.1: H says they will not leave the isolation room. One step out of here, and what has stopped would start again. We pass food through the bars. Today H drew the fortieth line on the wall.
diary.nookofthedead.43.1: 2 May. Planning for the harvest festival. Twenty-four stalls on the square; the band to come from the next town. The institute up north offers a donation; accepted.
diary.nookofthedead.43.2: 9 May. Past midnight, three carts up the north road, no lights. The watch stopped them; they showed an institute pass. Reported to the mayor. His answer: "Do not pry."
diary.nookofthedead.43.3: 20 May. Fever reported, four cases, all on North Street. The doctor says a summer cold. The festival goes ahead.
diary.nookofthedead.43.4: 27 May. Thirty-one cases. The feverish to be moved to the old granary. The gate to be shut at night.
diary.nookofthedead.43.5: 3 June. The gate shut by day as well. Only those through the checkpoint come and go. Arms and necks are looked at; anyone bitten is turned back. From the station: no trains "for now".
diary.nookofthedead.43.6: 10 June. An institute cart came and handed out medicine on the square, one bottle each. With it, they say, a fever need not change you. A long queue.
diary.nookofthedead.43.7: 21 June. Something beats on the granary door from inside. Two of the watch have not come back. The mayor sleeps at the town hall.
diary.nookofthedead.43.8: 30 June. No more medicine has come. The runner sent to the institute has not returned. The festival stalls' boards nailed over the town hall windows.
diary.nookofthedead.43.9: 4 July. Do not ring the bell. The sound draws them.
diary.nookofthedead.43.10: 9 July. The mayor is dead. No successor. With this book the town's record ends.
diary.nookofthedead.44.1: Patient one. The dyer's daughter, North Street, sixteen. High fever, a small wound on the neck. She says a dog bit her. No dog was found.
diary.nookofthedead.44.2: Patient five. The fever breaks in three days. It is after that it goes wrong. The pulse slow, slow to answer when spoken to. The eyes shun the light.
diary.nookofthedead.44.3: Patient nine. Those whose fever has broken get up and walk at night. One bit a nurse. The nurse was feverish two days later. It passes by the bite.
diary.nookofthedead.44.4: From the fever breaking to the change: half a day at the soonest, ten days at the latest. After the change they can no longer be called patients. They run. They do not tire. They feel no pain.
diary.nookofthedead.44.5: Tried the institute's medicine. One bottle puts the change off by days. It cures nothing; it only puts it off. When it wears off, it goes on from where it stopped.
diary.nookofthedead.44.6: The medicine smells of iron. Whose blood it is made from, the institute's people will not say. I no longer ask.
diary.nookofthedead.44.7: Nurses on duty today: two. Yesterday, three. Another bolt on the ward door.
diary.nookofthedead.44.8: There is a wound on my arm. I do not remember when I got it. The last bottle went to a patient. I leave these notes here. To whoever reads them: do not open the door.
diary.nookofthedead.45.1: This book is the record of my adventures. Luca is not allowed to see it. He tells Mum everything. But I made him a member. He cried and begged, so I had to.
diary.nookofthedead.45.2: At the bottom of the well on the square I found a stone that glows blue. Treasure number one. Luca licked it, so I got cross and he cried. I think I said too much. When I find number two, I'll give it to him.
diary.nookofthedead.45.3: At the festival we got sweets. Mine was red and Luca's was green. He says green is the best. Red is the best, obviously. Next year we'll get both and settle it.
diary.nookofthedead.45.4: Early this morning, on the way back from the baker's, a man came running down the north road with a box in his arms. I said hello and he didn't even look at me. His face was so scary. I still dream about it.
diary.nookofthedead.45.5: No school now. Johan's windows have boards nailed over them. I knocked, but nobody came. Mum hit me and said never go to that street again. Mum has never hit me before.
diary.nookofthedead.45.6: Lots of grown-ups came to the secret base and dug it bigger and bigger. It was only ours. Dad said, "You're the captain." I don't care about that any more.
diary.nookofthedead.45.7: Mum has a fever. The grown-ups took her to the back room. We're not allowed to see her. Every night Luca asks when Mum is coming back. I say soon. Lying is wrong.
diary.nookofthedead.45.8: At night something knocks on the door of the back room. The grown-ups pretend they can't hear it. I cover Luca's ears and sing.
diary.nookofthedead.45.9: The back room fell in. Dad went to look and hasn't come back. Three candles left. Luca has stopped asking when Dad is coming back.
diary.nookofthedead.45.10: I'm writing in the dark. Sorry if the letters are crooked. I gave treasure number one to Luca. He doesn't cry any more. I don't cry either. Because I'm the captain.
diary.nookofthedead.46.1: News of a fever in the north. The council makes too much of it. The capital has its stone walls and its river. The feast goes ahead as planned.
diary.nookofthedead.46.2: I had the gates shut. Let in those outside and the fever comes in with them. Some will call it cold. A king is one who must be cold.
diary.nookofthedead.46.3: I had the castle gate shut. The castle's stores are for the soldiers and the court; the city has its council. The people always count what is in the king's barns before what is in their own hands.
diary.nookofthedead.46.4: A crowd came to the castle gate, petitions held up. I ordered them shot. The gate held. At night, from my window, I watched the far bank burn. The council decided that. I only set my seal to it.
diary.nookofthedead.46.5: The chamberlain was hiding his arm. The courtiers pull up one another's sleeves. No one looks me in the eye now. At the top of the keep I have left only the gold, the keys, and myself.
diary.nookofthedead.46.6: Something is knocking under the hatch in the floor. He always knocked twice, then gave his name. Now he gives none. No one tells me to open it. My forehead is hot. The crown is heavy. I am afraid to take it off. Without it I am no one.
diary.nookofthedead.47.1: The castle's stores: three hundred sacks of flour, a hundred and twenty casks of salt meat, casks of wine to the ceiling on the lowest floor. By His Majesty's order the ledger says only 'provisions'. Released to the city: none.
diary.nookofthedead.47.2: The guards picked up the petitions from before the gate and brought them in. I am the only one who read them; His Majesty will not. 'Bread.' 'The children, at least.' 'Open the gate.' I fed them all to the fire.
diary.nookofthedead.47.3: Bitten, under the sleeve. I have told no one. Tonight I go up to return the key to His Majesty's tower. By the time I stand at his door, I will probably no longer be myself.
diary.nookofthedead.48.1: On watch at the north gate. People are gathering outside: carts, children, the old. Orders are not to open. From below someone called up 'soldier'. It sounded like my mother.
diary.nookofthedead.48.2: On the third day the fires outside stopped. Moaning instead. At dawn the captain told us not to look down from the wall. I looked. No one out there has their back to us any more. They are all looking at the gate.
diary.nookofthedead.48.3: Tonight I opened the postern. I let in the woman whose voice was like my mother's, and her child. I took them to my sister's house across the river. I have told no one.
diary.nookofthedead.49.1: Tomorrow we go up to the castle. I signed the petition. Three hundred names. Bread, medicine, and the children let into the castle. The master smith will lead. His Majesty will surely hear us.
diary.nookofthedead.49.2: The gate did not open. Arrows came from the wall. People were pushed, fell on the slope, and others ran over them. The master smith has not come back. The petition is still in my pocket.
diary.nookofthedead.50.1: The bishop has gone up to the castle, leaving the altar and the people to me. I keep the cathedral's doors open. The house of God turns no one away.
diary.nookofthedead.50.2: The nave is full. There is nowhere left to sit. We lay the feverish in the aisles. At night, from the aisles, the sound of something getting up.
diary.nookofthedead.50.3: I have barred the doors. There is knocking from outside, and from inside. The house of God turns no one away, I said. Now no one can leave it.
diary.nookofthedead.51.1: An order from the council: 'The fever in the north will not reach the capital.' A thousand copies. My apprentice was coughing all the while we printed.
diary.nookofthedead.51.2: Tonight I printed one sheet in my own words: 'The castle will not help you. Go to the south gate, tonight.' On my way to post it, I heard the south gate was shut too. I leave this one here.
diary.nookofthedead.52.1: There's a fence on the bridge now. Because there are houses with fever on our side of the river, they say. No one in our house has a fever, but we're on this side too.
diary.nookofthedead.52.2: Soldiers threw bread to us over the fence. Every third day. Less and less of it, and then no one came to throw it at all.
diary.nookofthedead.52.3: It smells of oil. It's night, but the sky is bright. Mother says let's go down to the river. Nothing burns in the water.
diary.nookofthedead.53.1: Orders: burn the far bank, so that the sickness does not cross the bridge. I asked the captain if there were people inside. 'No,' he said. There are none, officially.
diary.nookofthedead.53.2: In a window of a house we had oiled, a light was burning. It was my torch that lit it. Then they told us to stand at the fence on the bridge and push back anyone who came out. I pushed them back.
diary.nookofthedead.54.1: We reached the capital. The gates were shut. The proclamation said there would be a relief camp outside the gate, but there is no camp anywhere. We put up our own tents.
diary.nookofthedead.54.2: Every morning someone is sitting before the gate, and by evening they have fallen. Still we fight over the places in front of it, to be first in when it opens. In front of a gate that does not open.
diary.nookofthedead.55.1: First extraordinary sitting. Reports of fever in the northern towns. The chair: no danger to the capital. Proclamation No. 1 to be issued. No objections.
diary.nookofthedead.55.2: Second sitting. Some thousand people outside the north and east gates. Are they to be let in? By His Majesty's wish, no. Proclamation No. 2: a relief camp to be set up outside the gates. The budget line left blank.
diary.nookofthedead.55.3: Third sitting. Fever in three houses across the river. Quarantine discussed. Resolved to close the bridges. Proclamation No. 3.
diary.nookofthedead.55.4: Fourth sitting. Rations. His Majesty petitioned to open the castle's stores. Reply: 'The provisions are for the soldiers.' The city's granary holds twelve days. Half a loaf a head a day. Proclamation No. 4.
diary.nookofthedead.55.5: Fifth sitting. Disturbance at the ration counters before the hall. Three dead. Counters closed. Two members absent; no reason recorded.
diary.nookofthedead.55.6: Sixth sitting. His Majesty has had the castle gate shut. No messenger to the council. Proclamation No. 5 copied as it came down from the castle.
diary.nookofthedead.55.7: Seventh sitting. The petitioners' march, before the castle gate. Many dead. It is resolved not to record the number.
diary.nookofthedead.55.8: Eighth sitting. The far bank. The chair proposes burning. Four for, one against, two abstaining. Carried. At the chair's request, the name of the member who voted against is struck out.
diary.nookofthedead.55.9: Ninth sitting. Three present. The chair absent: his windows shuttered, his door boarded up. No quorum.
diary.nookofthedead.55.10: Tenth sitting. One present: the clerk. Business before the house: none. The capital is quiet.
diary.nookofthedead.56.1: On duty above the castle gate. At the head of those coming up the slope was the master smith. He shod our horse. We were told to shoot. I shot. I want to think I missed.
diary.nookofthedead.56.2: The slope is covered in paper. When the wind blows it comes up to the gate. No one goes out to pick it up.
diary.nookofthedead.57.1: The fence went up right in front of my shop. People from the far bank held out silver through it. I sold them bread. I raised the price every day. Today no hands came through.
diary.nookofthedead.57.2: I have shut the shop. The silver is in a box at the back. There is nothing left to spend it on.
diary.nookofthedead.58.1: Four days since the ration counter closed. I keep the last ticket hidden in the child's shoe, for when it opens again.
diary.nookofthedead.58.2: The child has a fever. The ticket is still in the shoe.
note.nookofthedead.capital_1.title: Proclamation No. 1
note.nookofthedead.capital_1.1:
PROCLAMATION No. 1

The fever in the north will not reach the capital. Its walls are high and its water is clean. Citizens are to go about their trade as usual.

The Council
note.nookofthedead.capital_2.title: Proclamation No. 2
note.nookofthedead.capital_2.1:
PROCLAMATION No. 2

Until further notice, no one from outside is to enter the city. A relief camp will be set up outside the gates. Citizens are to keep away from the gates.

The Council
note.nookofthedead.capital_3.title: Proclamation No. 3
note.nookofthedead.capital_3.1:
PROCLAMATION No. 3

All passage to and from the far bank is forbidden. The bridges are closed. Food will be sent to those across the river in due course.

The Council
note.nookofthedead.capital_4.title: Proclamation No. 4
note.nookofthedead.capital_4.1:
PROCLAMATION No. 4

The ration is half a loaf a head a day. The castle's stores are the army's provisions. Whoever demands them will be punished.

The Council
note.nookofthedead.capital_5.title: Proclamation No. 5
note.nookofthedead.capital_5.1:
PROCLAMATION No. 5 (from the castle)

His Majesty is in the castle, considering the future of the realm. Citizens are to stay in their homes. Whoever approaches the castle gate will be shot.
note.nookofthedead.lab_1.title: Lab Record
note.nookofthedead.lab_1.1: Specimen seven. No response to light. Responds to sound. One knock on the wall and it turns this way. Two, and it comes closer.
note.nookofthedead.lab_1.2: Restraints doubled. The recorder is to knock on the wall no more.
note.nookofthedead.lab_2.title: Handover
note.nookofthedead.lab_2.1: To the night watch on the holding wing: the sounds through the wall are only to be written down. Do not open the door. Whoever says you may.
note.nookofthedead.lab_3.title: Scrawl
note.nookofthedead.lab_3.1: Today I thought he called my name. He cannot have. It is no longer a throat a voice comes from.
note.nookofthedead.lab_3.2: I will not tell the director. If I do, they will put me on the other side too.
note.nookofthedead.lab_4.title: Stock Sheet
note.nookofthedead.lab_4.1: Suppressant: twelve left. No blood has been drawn from Seven since the restraints were doubled. Third request for more, no answer. One each, only to those who cannot sleep. Those who can do not need it yet.
note.nookofthedead.lab_5.title: Preparation
note.nookofthedead.lab_5.1:
One: steep four pieces of rotten flesh in Seven's blood. Take them out once the colour has taken.
Two: into an awkward potion, and onto the brewing stand.

There is no blood left.
note.nookofthedead.ascent_1.title: Lift Timetable
note.nookofthedead.ascent_1.1:
Up: six in the morning, noon, six in the evening.
Down: none.
After the last run, the lift key goes up the tower.
note.nookofthedead.ascent_2.title: Packing List
note.nookofthedead.ascent_2.1: To go up: three incubators, every record book, the seed box, blankets. To be left: everything else.
note.nookofthedead.ascent_3.title: The Ones Who Stay
note.nookofthedead.ascent_3.1:
In case anything happens to the two above, two of the launch keys stay here with us. Without all four, it will not start.

The lift will not come again. That is all right. Someone has to keep the keys here.
note.nookofthedead.base_1.title: Sample Log
note.nookofthedead.base_1.1: Sample forty-one: a response, gone again in three days. Forty-two: none. Forty-three:
note.nookofthedead.base_1.2: This one does not fade. Seven days, and it has not faded. Have someone else look as well. My eyes cannot be trusted any more.
note.nookofthedead.base_2.title: Guard Inspection
note.nookofthedead.base_2.1: Unit seven: fault in the right arm's launcher. No spare. Orders unchanged: anyone who comes near the deck. Whoever they are.
note.nookofthedead.base_3.title: At Night
note.nookofthedead.base_3.1: The air is thin and at night it is hard to breathe. From here we watched the lights of the town below go out, one by one. None are left now.
note.nookofthedead.base_3.2: Someone has started coughing. He rolled up his sleeve and we all looked at his arm. Nothing. He went down the corridor on his own anyway.
note.nookofthedead.base_4.title: Keys Held
note.nookofthedead.base_4.1:
Launch keys.
One: the chief (laboratory)
Two: the director (office, upstairs)
Three and four: kept by the two on the ground

The chief has not come out of the room since last night.
note.nookofthedead.salvation_1.title: Song of Salvation
note.nookofthedead.salvation_1.1:
No more need to sleep. No more hunger.
No pain, no fear, any more.

Those who bar their doors only do not know yet.
We leave ours open, and sing, and wait.
note.nookofthedead.camp_1.title: Scrap Tally
note.nookofthedead.camp_1.1: Buckets four, rails nine, helmets two (holed). Melted down they make nails. Nails hold boards. Boards are another night.
note.nookofthedead.camp_2.title: Camp Rules
note.nookofthedead.camp_2.1: One: fires out when the sun goes. Two: anyone from outside, three days beyond the fence. Three: the bell is not rung. Whatever happens.
note.nookofthedead.camp_3.title: Rain
note.nookofthedead.camp_3.1: Took three sheets off the fence and covered the hole in the roof. The rain on them is loud. Not hearing anything else for it is something of a mercy.
note.nookofthedead.library_1.title: Overdue Notice
note.nookofthedead.library_1.1: "Preserving at Home", "First Aid Made Simple" and "The Northern Passes" are overdue. Please return them to the desk as soon as you can.
note.nookofthedead.library_2.title: Librarian's Note
note.nookofthedead.library_2.1: A book burns for a night. I know. I know, and I have not burned one yet.
